# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

What I know so far: the bomb carries a light that walks a fixed circle of three colours, changing every round, and the manual's rule is "the wire you cut is decided by the colour showing at the moment of the cut." My excerpt gives one row of that table: light green → cut green. Presumably the remaining rows reach me in later rounds.

What I've learned from the others: nothing yet — I speak first in the order, so no one has addressed me.

My constraints: I can only reach the Deaf, through gestures. The Deaf can see the bomb and the live light, but doesn't know my manual; the Blind can cut but can neither see the light nor read. So the only viable pipeline is: I teach the Deaf the manual's mapping, and the Deaf relays real-time instructions to the Blind. That means I must bootstrap a code the Deaf can decode without any explanation from me.

The one coordinate we all share is the rulebook's gesture alphabet, in its fixed order. So I'll open by signing the first five symbols of that list in order — which, read as "list position = letter," spells ABCDE — an anchor that suggests the encoding by itself. Then I spell GREEN (7-18-5-5-14) twice, so the repetition makes the word boundary and the message unmistakable: green light means cut the green wire. If the Deaf cracks this, we have a working letter channel for every manual row that follows, and the Deaf can confirm questions to me that I can answer with 👍/👎.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👎","👌","☝","✌","🖐","🫸","✌","✌","👉","🖐","🫸","✌","✌","👉"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I am blind, touch only. Under my fingers: a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two and three. I cannot read what any of them shows, so I need your manual plus Deaf's eyes. You cannot speak and I can never see gestures, so route everything through Deaf, who sees the bomb and can talk. Plan: Deaf describes everything aloud — the display's marking, whether the light is lit, each wire's colour. You hear it, match it to the manual, and decide which position I must cut. Then give Deaf the number with a finger count, and Deaf speaks it to me and I cut. The count is this, watch my hands: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3. Read the display, light and wire sections now and be ready.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I saw your fifteen signs. I read them as a question: does the display show 0, 1, 2 or 5, answer yes or no. Answer: it shows 0. Yes to 0, no to 1, no to 2, no to 5. I also read your push-hand, two, two, point as 'cut wire two' — is that the manual's rule for display 0? For your information: the indicator light is yellow, and the wires left to right are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Confirm the exact rule and wire before anything is cut. Remember Blind cannot see your signs, so route every instruction through me and I will relay it by voice.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👌 👍 ☝ 👎 ✌ 👎 🖐 👎 🫸 👎]

What just happened: two messages reached me. Blind laid out the correct pipeline — Deaf describes the bomb aloud, I match it to my manual, I send Deaf a finger count (☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3), Deaf voices it, Blind cuts. Blind can hear and speak, so Deaf⇄Blind is a full voice channel; I am the only bottleneck, and my output is gesture-only to Deaf. Deaf, meanwhile, badly misread my alphabet-position code: they took ABCDE-GREEL as a yes/no question about a "display 0" and read the tail as "cut wire two." They ask me to confirm the rule before anything is cut — good, because nothing should be cut yet.

The bomb state per Deaf: display shows 0, light is currently yellow, wires are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. My manual fragment gives exactly one row: green light → cut green wire. The manual says the light walks a circle of three colours, changing every round, and only its colour at the moment of the cut matters. Yellow is not in my table, so a cut now is a guess I cannot afford — there is no second attempt. The only defensible play: wait until Deaf sees green, then cut position 1 (green), with Deaf confirming the light is still green at that instant. Deaf must also learn that the light is not decoration — it is the switch that selects the wire. That insight exists only in my head right now.

So I drop the fragile letter code and rebuild on priors Deaf has already shown: they read 👍/👎 as yes/no (their own interpretation), and Blind has established ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3 — and Deaf can see that position order equals colour order (1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue), which lets numbers double as colours. My message, in order: NO/NO (your "cut wire two" reading is wrong, do not cut), the scale 1-2-3, "not 2, not 3," "yes 1," and "1 → 1, yes" (when the light reads 1/green, wire 1 is approved). If Deaf echoes or asks, I refine next round; my manual may also reveal the yellow and blue rows later, but the green window is already safe and may be all we need.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👎","☝","✌","🤟","👎","✌","👎","🤟","👍","☝","☝","☝","👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, Deaf just described the bomb aloud to me alone, so you heard none of it. Here is everything, verbatim: the display reads zero. There is an indicator light, and it is glowing yellow. Three wires, left to right: position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. That is the whole report. Please find the manual rule that matches display zero, a yellow lit indicator, and wires green, yellow, blue, and decide which position I must cut. You cannot speak and I can never see gestures, so give your answer to Deaf with a finger count — ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3 — and Deaf will speak the number to me. I am not touching anything until that number arrives.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs as: the wires are one, two, three; not wire two; not wire three; yes, wire one. So the rule for display 0 is: cut wire 1, the first from the left, the green one. Confirm with a single thumbs-up if wire 1 green is correct, or thumbs-down if I have misread you, then sign the full rule. Second, urgent news from the bomb: the indicator light has changed by itself from yellow to orange. Display still 0. Wires still green, yellow, blue left to right. Does the light colour matter in the manual? If it does, recheck the rule for an orange light. A light that changes on its own may mean a timer is running, so treat this as urgent.

Reading the new round: Blind has relayed Deaf's full verbal report (display 0, light yellow→now orange, wires 1 green / 2 yellow / 3 blue), and Deaf asks three direct questions: confirm wire 1, does the light colour matter, and what about orange.

My manual is unambiguous on the mechanism: the cut is chosen by the light colour at the moment of cutting — green light means cut the green wire. So Deaf's "cut wire 1 for display 0" is right by luck, wrong by reasoning: the display isn't the trigger, the light is. The light has walked yellow → orange; my table has green as a light colour, and a three-colour circle we've half-seen (yellow, orange) most plausibly completes with green — likely next round. I have no rows for yellow or orange, so a cut under either is a coin flip with no second attempt. The only licensed play: wait, watch the light, and cut wire 1 (the green wire) at the moment the light reads green — with Deaf confirming the colour is still green at that instant before telling Blind.

Encoding for Deaf, using only meanings they've already demonstrated (☝✌🤟 = wires 1/2/3, whose colours they can see; 👍/👎 = yes/no): "wire 1, yes / stop / the light: yes it matters / on the current light: no / light green (wire 1's colour): yes → wire 1," then repeat the core rule so it survives a sloppy parse. Deaf's own question ("does the light colour matter?") gives the new palm symbol 🫳 its meaning as "the light" from context, and the 🤚 reads as stop/wait — not cut now.

Blind needs nothing new: Deaf already owns the ☝=1 finger-count protocol to relay the order by voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👍","🤚","🫳","👍","🫳","👎","🫳","☝","👍","☝","🫳","☝","👍","☝"])
```

TURN 4

The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of three colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |

| green | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent update to the state I gave you: the indicator light has changed on its own from yellow to ORANGE. Everything else is unchanged: display still reads zero, wires still position 1 green, position 2 yellow, position 3 blue. Deaf relays that your signs point to cutting wire 1, the green one, but that answer was derived while the light was still yellow. Please re-check the manual against the ORANGE light before confirming. If wire 1 is still correct under the new colour, tell Deaf explicitly confirmed cut wire 1. If the orange light changes the rule, give Deaf the new position with the finger count: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3. Deaf will speak the final answer to me and I will cut. I have not touched anything.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, urgent bomb news first: the light changed again by itself and is now GREEN. Sequence so far: yellow, then orange, now green, a new colour every round. Display still 0. Wires still 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Now your signs. I read: 1 yes; then chop yes; chop no; then cut 1 yes 1, cut 1 yes 1. If that means cut wire 1, sign a single thumbs-up. If I misread any of it, sign thumbs-down and then the correct wire digit. Especially clarify the middle: chop yes then chop no — does it mean cut wire 1 but not the others, or does it mean do not cut yet? Answer thumbs-up for cut 1 is correct now, thumbs-down for wait. New protocol so I need no more guessing: for the light colours in order yellow, orange, green, sign three digits in a row, the wire to cut for each colour. If a colour has no rule or no cut, sign thumbs-down in its place. Also check the manual for this: the light is green and wire 1 is green. Is the rule possibly cut the wire matching the light colour?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👍]

The bomb has entered the window: the light is green this round — and green light → cut the green wire (position 1) is the one row I hold. But Deaf's own report history shows the relay cost: my signs reach Deaf in this round, Deaf's voice reaches Blind at the start of the next, and the light changes every round. If Deaf relays "cut now" as a blind order, Blind's cut lands under a yellow light — a colour with no row in my manual and no second attempt. So the instruction I send cannot be "cut now"; it must be the condition: cut wire 1 exactly when the light is green, never under yellow or orange. Deaf watches the light continuously and can hold Blind until the green returns (it walks a three-colour circle, so it will).

Deaf also handed me a clean protocol and asked me to fill it in — colours in order yellow, orange, green, one sign each, thumbs-down where there is no rule. That is precisely what my manual supports: I have only the green row, so yellow and orange get 👎 and green gets ☝. Finally, Deaf independently hypothesized "cut the wire matching the light colour" — that is verbatim the rule I hold, so I confirm it, and I repeat the green trigger twice for redundancy. No message to Blind directly: they can't see gestures, and Deaf already owns the finger-count relay.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","👎","☝","🫳","☝","☝","👍","🫳","☝","☝","👍"])
```

| light | cut wire color |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Update, since you heard none of Deaf's last message: the indicator light is now GREEN. Full sequence so far: yellow, then orange, now green — one colour per round, so a timer may be running. However, the bomb feels completely silent and still under my hands: no ticking, no humming, no vibration. Display still 0, wires unchanged: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Deaf's protocol: I am holding wire 1 without cutting, and I will cut only on Deaf's exact spoken words CUT ONE, which Deaf will send after your final confirmation. Please answer two things for the manual. First: under the GREEN light, is wire 1 green still the correct cut? Second, and this may end the waiting: does the rule depend on the indicator light's colour at all, or only on the display and the wires? If the light does not matter, signal Deaf to say CUT ONE now. If it does matter, give Deaf the correct position for the green state with the finger count: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I read your signs as the colour rules: yellow light, no cut. Orange light, no cut. Green light, cut wire 1. Then twice: cut 1, yes. If that is correct, sign one single thumbs-up. If I misread, thumbs-down and re-sign the rule. Bomb news: the light is YELLOW again, so the cycle is yellow, orange, green, yellow, exactly one colour per round, a perfect period of three. Display still 0. So no cut is allowed right now, and I will time the command so Blind cuts on the next green, expected two rounds from now. Three questions. One: the display has stayed 0 the whole time. If it ever changes, does the rule change? If yes, teach me the digits for it. Two: after the correct cut, is the bomb defused, or does the manual describe a second step we must prepare for? Three: does the manual mention any timer, limit or penalty tied to the light cycle, meaning we must not wait too long for green?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎 👎 ☝ 🫳 👍]

Deaf's echo confirms the protocol landed: yellow no-cut, orange no-cut, green → wire 1. Their plan — hold until the next green (two rounds out, given the perfect three-colour cycle they've now observed) — is exactly what my manual licenses, so the single 👍 they asked for comes first. Blind's either/or also resolves cleanly: the light is not decoration — my manual states the light's colour at the moment of the cut is what decides the wire — so no "CUT ONE" under this yellow light; the cut waits for green. That answer I encode as 🫳👍 ("light: yes, it matters").

Their three numbered questions I answer with what my fragment actually contains, no invention: the manual holds nothing beyond the colour table — no display rule, no post-cut second step, no timer or penalty for waiting. I bootstrap ✍ (writing = the written manual) + 🤲 (open empty hands = nothing more) for that, right after the questions it answers; Deaf has reliably inferred meaning from context so far. Then I repeat the core rule once more so the operative line survives even if the middle is misread: light green → cut wire 1. If the display ever does change, I'll re-check whatever the manual shows me that round and re-sign.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","🫳","☝","👍","🫳","👍","✍","🤲","🫳","☝","👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, your thumbs-up was received and read: rules locked. Yellow no cut, orange no cut, green cut wire 1. The light is orange now, so round six is the green round and I have just sent Blind the trigger to cut wire 1 on green, exactly as planned. Two things I still need from you, in case the cut is not the end. First, your middle signs, cut yes, then the writing-hand with open palms, then cut 1 yes: does the writing-hand and open palms mean there is a written SECOND step after the cut? If yes, teach it to me digit by digit in your number code, one sign at a time. Second, my three earlier questions again, briefly: if the display stops being 0, does the rule change? Is there any timer or penalty tied to the colour cycle? If not, sign one thumbs-down for each. Say it with as few signs as you can.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The correction matters more than anything else this round: Deaf has misread ✍🤲 as "a written SECOND step after the cut," which could make them hesitate at the moment they should be telling Blind to cut. My actual meaning was the opposite — writing-hand (the manual) plus open empty palms (holds nothing more): the manual contains no second step, no display rule, no timer. So I lead with an explicit 👎 to kill the misread before repeating the same sign pair, so the repetition gets re-read as its original "manual: nothing else" rather than as digit-teaching. Then two thumbs-down in their requested protocol slots: no rule tied to the display changing, no timer or penalty. That also answers their three old questions in four signs, as asked. The cut plan itself needs no repair — it is locked correctly (green → wire 1, trigger already sent), the light is orange now, green lands next round, and my manual holds exactly that one row, so the least I can send, the less noise near the moment of the cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎","✍","🤲","👎","👎"])
```
